ShieldKey is built so your data stays yours. Here is how — no jargon.
No Internet permission. Nothing ever leaves your phone. No account, no server — nothing to hack remotely.
Military-grade and authenticated: if a single byte is altered or the key is wrong, opening simply fails.
AES-256 · GCM · 128-bit tag · random IV per item
Your master password is turned into a key by Argon2id — \"memory-hard\", designed to be slow and costly to crack at scale (anti-GPU/ASIC), far tougher than PBKDF2.
Your master password is stored nowhere. It only unlocks an internal random key. No one — not even the developer — can open your vault without your password.
If you forget your master password, only YOUR recovery code (the one you wrote down) can restore the vault. No email, no recovery server — no backdoor.

Fingerprint: the unlocking key lives in your phone\'s secure chip and never leaves it. Registering a new fingerprint destroys that key — so nobody can enrol their own finger to get in. On a phone with no sensor, the screen code is used instead, and quick unlock is then only as strong as that code.
Android Keystore / TEE / StrongBox · destroyed on new enrolment

When you copy a secret, it is flagged \"sensitive\" (hidden from clipboard history on Android 13+) and cleared when you lock the vault. The 45-second timer only works while ShieldKey is open: Android forbids background apps from touching the clipboard. Locking the vault is what clears it for certain.
Android refuses to capture ShieldKey, and the app preview stays hidden in the recent-apps list. A screen-recording app captures nothing.
Each document is encrypted separately and stays usable even with no connection.
🎣 We will never ask for your info
ShieldKey will never email or text you to ask for your password or data. If someone does, it is not us.
No vault protects against everything. Here is what falls outside — said plainly, so you know where the real risk sits.

If you type your card number into a fake site, you hand it over yourself. ShieldKey has no Internet access: it cannot see web pages and cannot warn you. Best defence: a virtual card with a spending limit — a single-use number is worthless to a thief.
Your card is copied from their database, without you doing anything wrong. Nothing on your phone can prevent it. What helps: knowing which cards you gave to whom, so you can react fast.

A keylogger or a rogue accessibility service sees everything you type or display — in any app, ours included. ShieldKey limits the damage (nothing leaves, nothing is captured, nothing lingers in the clipboard) but cannot repair a compromised phone.

If someone takes over your phone line, they intercept the SMS that validates a payment. This plays out between your bank and your operator. Prefer validation through your banking app rather than by SMS.

⚠️ This phone appears to be rooted

Root access (su, Magisk…) was detected. On such a phone, any app you grant root to can read ShieldKey\'s files, its memory while the vault is open, or what you type. Encryption still holds: with the vault closed, the file stays unreadable without your password. But ShieldKey can neither prevent what root allows, nor guarantee this detection — it can be hidden. The risk is yours to judge.

While ShieldKey is on screen, Android 12 and later forbids other apps from drawing over it. A fake password field laid over the real one, or an invisible button under your finger — the favourite trick of banking trojans — cannot appear.
